pages.note: Both versions follow the commentary on smokiness, grayness (not curd or sugar), substance-ness and blazing correctly. Both blur the closing ཡང་དག་པར་ལྡན་པ་ཅན་ཉིད་ལ་ལྡན་པ་ཅན་དག་ལ་ཁྱད་པར་མེད་པ (the conjoined are undifferentiated in conjunction) in a similar way, which is not serious.

A_serious.english: the relationship itself does not exist as a second entity
A_serious.problem: The reply says the relation does not reside in two things, because it is avinābhāva and applies only to the sign. A reads gnyis pa as 'a second entity', so the reply's actual claim is lost.

A_serious.english: then the sign-possessor is prevented from occurring elsewhere
A_serious.problem: The Tibetan says the sign-possessor occurring elsewhere is NOT negated by this restriction (p205 confirms: རྟགས་ཅན་ནི་རྟགས་ལས་གཞན་དུ་ཡོད་པ་དགག་པར་བྱ་བ་མ་ཡིན). A renders it as being prevented, which reverses it.

B_serious.english: establishes the core thesis regarding the expresser and the expressed
B_serious.problem: The Tibetan means the relation of what is made known and what makes it known (probandum/probans). 'Expresser and expressed' is brjod bya / rjod byed, so the inferential relation becomes a semantic one.

B_serious.class: wrong speaker / label read as claim
B_serious.english: The sign and the sign-possessor are like that; they appear to be identical in nature.
B_serious.problem: རང་བཞིན་ལྟར་སྣང་བ is the commentator's verdict that the opponent's argument is a pseudo-svabhāva reason. B folds it into the opponent's claim as an assertion of apparent identity.

pages.note: A reverses the final restriction (the sign-possessor occurring elsewhere is not negated) and misreads the 'not in two' reply. B's errors are lesser: a term slip and a mislabelled fallacy tag.

A_serious.english: Therefore, these are also what smoke makes known, whereas substantiality and the like are not
A_serious.problem: Grayness and the like are themselves provers (gamaka) of fire, because they occur only where there is fire. A makes them things that smoke makes known, which inverts the point of the second half of the verse.

A_serious.class: clause garbled so the reply loses its point
A_serious.english: just as the evidence occurs in the probandum, so too does the evidence occur in the other
A_serious.problem: The reply asserts mutuality on a shared locus: just as the sign-possessor occurs in the sign, so the sign occurs in the other. A makes both clauses about the evidence, so the objection is not answered.

B_serious.english: Therefore, these also make the smoke understood. However, qualities like "blazing" do not
B_serious.problem: Smoke makes substance-ness etc. known (as it does fireness), but not blazing. B has substance-ness making smoke known, which reverses probans and probandum.

B_serious.english: these are also what make the sign understood
B_serious.problem: Grayness etc. are provers of fire (the sign-possessor), not of the sign. The invented object 'the sign' confuses the argument, though B keeps them as provers.

pages.note: Each version reverses one of the two parallel smoke/fire statements: A gets the first (substance-ness) right and the second (grayness) wrong, B the reverse. A also garbles the mutuality reply.
